summary: Mr. Mosseri explores the historical development of Tisha B'Ab customs, tracing many current stringencies to the influence of the Abideseon, a group of mourners in Yerushalayim during the 9th to 11th centuries. He explains how these practices, which originated outside of the Talmudic tradition, were adopted by Hachamim and eventually spread through Italy to become part of the customs practiced by Clal Yisrael today.
questions: Where do the customs of the three weeks and nine days come from?
Why do we say the Nahem prayer in the Amidah?
Did the Hachamim always agree with the mourning practices of the Abideseon?
How did customs from Yerushalayim spread to Italy and the rest of the world?
Why do some people refrain from eating meat and drinking wine for different periods before Tisha B'Ab?
